title: A correction names the answer it corrects, so the last one to arrive never wins only because it arrived last
request: Package T2 of the team workspace plan (the review's P2, 'a withdrawn delay preserves an obsolete ETA'): correcting the kitchen's extra minutes from 8 back to 0 returned 'skipped' and kept 18:40, because the correction branch used truthiness. Distinguish absence from an explicit zero, give each correction a base revision, allow the same value again on another base, refuse a late correction on an older base with a visible 'please reconcile' reply, make an identical retry add nothing, propagate to the Business brief, and keep the original acceptance score on its original revision. Test 0 -> 8 -> 0 -> 8.
spec: dclab-core 0.170.0 (pure functions, no contract change; the event kinds team.correction.applied/refused and the ledger point team.correction_accept were declared with T5a in 0.169.0): team_work.correction_revision(snapshot, field, value, base_revision), read_correction, accept_correction(current, base, already_applied=) and CORRECTION_VERDICTS. dclab_rnd: teamspace/tools.py judge_correction (the stored task's current report, the correction id's earlier attempt, minutes 0-240, a base required once revised), _reconcile, _model_call (a stale base writes a skipped attempt and the reconcile reply), the model_call tool's base_revision and correction_id; teamspace/agents.py correct() (judged before the turn, events and ledger once per call, an overtaken apply re-judged as stale_base) and the specialist's correction step. No migration.
plan: write the core rule as pure functions with the 0 -> 8 -> 0 -> 8 cases, a repeated value on another base and a base that names no report as tests
make the corrected input revision carry the field, the value and the base, so an explicit zero is never the base snapshot
judge each correction on the stored task before the specialist's turn; apply supersedes, duplicate writes nothing, stale_base writes a skipped attempt and tells the requester to reconcile
record each judgment once (experience event and ledger point) and keep the acceptance task untouched
CHANGELOG and CORE_INTEGRATION; tests on files and PostgreSQL; independent review and fixes

decisions.decision: the base revision is part of the corrected input revision (snapshot;kitchen_minutes=0@r2), which is also the score's retry key
decisions.why: with the value alone, 'withdraw the delay' (0) is the uncorrected snapshot and the first estimate comes back as a duplicate; with the base, the same 8 minutes on r1 and on r3 are two corrections, and a resend of one of them is the same attempt

decisions.decision: a correction on an older base is refused (stale_base) and the requester reads 'please reconcile' in its thread, never merged
decisions.why: applying it would overwrite a newer answer it never saw; only the sender knows whether it still applies

decisions.decision: the rule stays in dclab-core as pure functions; the host reads the stored task and reports
decisions.why: the main product needs the same judgment on its own records, and a pure rule needs no schema change

decisions.decision: a base is required once the first report has been superseded (the review's finding 1)
decisions.why: a correction with no base was taken as based on the newest report, so a late resend of the first +8 overwrote the later withdrawal: the very case the package exists to stop

change: dclab_core/team_work.py (the T2 block: correction_revision, read_correction, accept_correction, CORRECTION_VERDICTS), CHANGELOG 0.170.0 bullet; dclab_rnd/teamspace/tools.py (CORRECTED, MAX_MINUTES, _tag, _tagged, judge_correction, _reconcile, _model_call, the model_call schema); dclab_rnd/teamspace/agents.py (correct, _correction_event, the specialist's correction step); docs/guides/CORE_INTEGRATION.md; tests/test_core_team_corrections.py (new) and tests/test_teamspace_agents.py (_Corrections).

findings.defect: withdrawing the kitchen's delay kept the obsolete 18:40 estimate
findings.scenario: dispatch at 18:00, estimate 18:32; +8 minutes gives 18:40; correcting back to 0 returned 'skipped' and 18:40 stayed the current report
findings.cause: the correction branch tested the minutes by truthiness, so 0 read as 'no correction' and the input revision was the base snapshot, whose score already existed
findings.fix: correction_revision carries the field, the value and the base revision; 0 is an explicit value

findings.defect: the owner's-sequence test expected one ledger row fewer than the code records
findings.scenario: the late stale_base correction is sent twice; the second sending happened after the ledger patch's with-block had ended
findings.cause: the expectation was wrong, not the code: each call is judged and recorded once, and only calls inside the patch are seen
findings.fix: the expectation counts the calls inside the patch and the experience events count both sendings

findings.defect: a correction with no base was never stale
findings.scenario: +8 (r2), then 0 (r3, delay withdrawn); the first +8 arrives late with no base and no id: it was taken as 8@r3, applied, and r4 said 18:40 again
findings.cause: a missing base defaulted to the current report's revision
findings.fix: judge_correction refuses a correction with no base (and no known correction id) once the first report is superseded

findings.defect: of two corrections on one base, the one that lost the race was reported as applied and nobody was told
findings.scenario: A (5@r1) and B (8@r1) both judged apply; B's score finishes after A reported r2: no report, no event, no reconcile reply, but verdict 'apply'
findings.cause: correct() returned early when an apply made no report
findings.fix: a scored apply that made no report because the report moved on is re-judged stale_base, recorded as refused and the requester gets the reconcile reply (keyed per attempt, so once)

findings.defect: correction id 'k' matched the earlier attempt of id 'k:2'
findings.scenario: 'k:2' (+8) applied; 'k' (+9, base 2) was refused as 'already given for another correction'
findings.cause: the tag was matched with startswith(tag + ':') and a safe id may contain ':'
findings.fix: the tag ends with ': ' (a safe id has no space)

findings.defect: negative or very large minutes were accepted
findings.scenario: -40 gave an arrival before the dispatch estimate; 1500 wrapped past midnight
findings.cause: no bound on the minutes in correct() or the tool schema
findings.fix: 0 to 240 minutes in judge_correction and in the model_call schema

findings.defect: a zero with no delay to withdraw was recorded as 'already_applied', and the reconcile reply invited a resend with the same id, which is refused
findings.scenario: first correction 0 on r1; a stale correction resent against the current report under its old id
findings.cause: one reason code for every duplicate; the reply did not say a new correction id is needed
findings.fix: reason 'unchanged' for a no-op; the reply asks for a new correction against the current report

measurements.name: the review's findings as tests, before their fixes
measurements.gate: every new or extended test fails before its fix and passes after
measurements.result: 5 failing before (no base applied, -40 applied, 'k' refused, race reported apply, reason already_applied); 0 after

measurements.name: the T2 test groups on files and on PostgreSQL
measurements.gate: test_teamspace_agents, test_core_team_corrections, test_team_acceptance, test_team_target, test_teamspace_delivery, test_teamspace_store, test_lead_workspace, test_team_screens pass in both modes

outcome: A correction of a team's answer names the report revision it is based on: 0 -> 8 -> 0 -> 8 makes four revisions, a repeat adds nothing, a late one on an older base (or one overtaken on the same base) is refused with a visible reconcile reply, the Business brief shows the current value and the acceptance score keeps its revision. Not done: a crash between the report and its 'applied' event leaves that event missing (a resend records only a duplicate); a dispatch snapshot near 120 characters cannot be corrected (the revision's cap); no route lets a person send a correction from a thread yet; no live model run.
lessons: Never test a correction's value by truthiness: zero is the most common meaningful correction (a delay withdrawn).
A stale-base rule refuses only what states its base: a default base of 'the newest' silently turns every late resend into an apply.
When a judgment can change between judging and writing, re-judge at the end and record what actually happened, not what was planned.
risks: Requiring a base once revised makes every caller track the revision it saw; a caller that does not is refused, never guessed for.
Event recording is best effort: a crash after the report and before the event loses the applied event.
